summary: The right silhouette is there — stepped base, column, collar, glazed lantern, finial — so it clears programmer art, but the lantern is a chunky undetailed box, the column is a bare cylinder with no visible fluting, and a stray grey slab sits in the foreground of every view like an abandoned placeholder. It is a recognisable lamp, not a good one.

defects.fix: Delete the slab, or if a plinth is wanted, make it deliberate: a 10x0.5x10 dark stone pad with a 0.4-stud chamfered edge directly under the base, and re-frame the hero camera so the lamp fills ~40% of frame height, centered.
defects.observed: A large flat grey slab sits on the ground in the lower-left of the hero and side views, completely unrelated to the lamp. It reads as a leftover placeholder part and dominates the foreground of every shot.

defects.fix: Move the camera to 8-10 studs from the base, pitch up ~15 degrees so the finial nearly touches the top of frame, and center the lamp horizontally.
defects.observed: The lamp occupies roughly 10% of the frame and sits off to the right with huge empty sky and ground around it. There is no focal hierarchy — the eye lands on the grey slab first.

defects.fix: Add a cast-iron ladder bar (0.2-stud rod) up the back of the column, a 0.3-stud-diameter crossbar under the lantern, and a decorative scroll bracket — even 3-4 small black parts sell 'Victorian'.
defects.observed: The lantern is a plain box: four flat cream rectangles for glass with no glazing bars, no top crown moulding beyond a flat cap, and the finial is a single thin spike. The column is a bare cylinder with one bulge for a collar.

defects.fix: Scale the lantern housing down ~20% (to roughly 3.5 studs wide) and lengthen the exposed column by 2-3 studs so the lantern reads as a cap, not a box on a stick.
defects.observed: The lantern housing is nearly as wide as the visible column is long, making it top-heavy and chunky. Real Victorian lamps have a lantern roughly 1/4 to 1/3 the height of the post above the collar; here it reads closer to half.

defects.fix: Replace the cylinder with a 12-sided fluted column (alternating 0.15-stud radial ribs) and make the collar a two-tier ring: 1.4-stud torus over a 1.1-stud ring, 0.3 studs tall each.
defects.observed: The 'fluted column' reads as a smooth cylinder — no fluting is visible at any angle. The decorative collar is a single small bulge rather than a layered ring assembly.
